answer: Work-history cost ramp. Each identity must accumulate ferrous hardware attestations before its bids clear, and the ramp steepens with every fresh identity from the same device pool, so a farm pays a rising tide of idle hardware time per clone. Sybils must forge months of simulated uptime on distinct serials, and the marginal cost per extra identity climbs superlinearly rather than flatly. The attacker's per-identity toll is real machine wear plus detection risk, not a one-time deposit.
